description: Build provenance for the RT-BE Series 'Reaper' firmware. Each published image is traceable to an exact, independently-reproducible source tree: apply the published patch series onto the pinned upstream base, then hash release/src/router. The CI workflow .github/workflows/verify-provenance.yml reproduces every 'verifiable' entry on each run.

base.note: The base pin never moves. Reaper changes are carried as the patches/ series, and upstream carry-forwards (e.g. Merlin 3006.102.8 -> v2.1.2) are cherry-picked, NOT rebased, so this base stays constant and the reproduction recipe below is stable across releases.
base.series_note: Applying the published patches/ series from this base reproduces every release's source. Two hashes are recorded per release: source_tree is the tree of the build commit on the RT-BE96U branch (what the firmware was actually built from); source_tree_from_series is what `git am --keep-cr patches/[0-9]*.patch` onto this base yields. They differ ONLY by three vendored openssh-sftp documentation files (README.md, SECURITY.md, .github/ci-status.md) that the series' *.md doc-hunk exclusion strips; no source or code file differs, and release/src-rt is identical. CI (verify-provenance.yml) checks source_tree_from_series.

toolchain.note: Bit-for-bit binary reproduction additionally requires the proprietary Broadcom/ASUS/Trend Micro prebuilt blobs that upstream ships in-tree and that cannot be re-hosted here; the SOURCE reproduction (release/src/router tree hash) is fully independent of them.

reproduce: git clone https://github.com/RMerl/asuswrt-merlin.ng && cd asuswrt-merlin.ng && git checkout a7ebfa133a && git am --keep-cr /path/to/patches/0001-*.patch .. /path/to/patches/<NNNN>-*.patch && git rev-parse HEAD:release/src/router  # == the release's source_tree['release/src/router']

releases.summary: Single-change release: a workaround for a Broadcom defect in the closed libnvram.so that can permanently wedge an nvram write while leaving the router otherwise up. _wlcsm_init() passes the ADDRESS of its saved-PID field to the internal netlink port allocator as the port-candidate out-parameter; on EADDRINUSE the allocator walks ten candidates and writes each back through that pointer, corrupting the saved PID. The next call sees saved_pid != getpid(), concludes the process forked, and re-initialises without closing the previous socket - leaking one netlink socket per pass until all ten candidates are gone, after which wlcsm_nvram_getall() retries the failing send without bound while holding the nvram mutex. Because the send path re-enters _wlcsm_init(), each retry redoes the whole socket-plus-ten-binds sequence: roughly sixteen syscalls per pass with no backoff, which burns a core in system time, floods stderr, and never completes the write. The trigger is PID reuse landing on a netlink port a long-lived process already holds, and the leaked ports then squat for the life of the stuck process, so it compounds with uptime and process churn. Caught live on metal 2026-08-11 and confirmed instruction-by-instruction in the shipped binary. The fix is a small LD_PRELOAD object of our own (the closed library is not modified): it interposes bind() and, only when the real call already failed EADDRINUSE on an AF_NETLINK protocol-31 socket with a non-zero nl_pid, retries once with nl_pid = 0 so the kernel autobinds - which is what Broadcom's own second WLCSM socket already does. Every step of the failure chain is gated on that first bind, so making it succeed removes all of it. SHIPS INERT: /etc/ld.so.preload is global to every dynamically linked process and this has not run on hardware, so the nvram flag defaults to 0 and no router behaviour changes until an operator sets wlcsm_bindfix=1. NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
releases.models_note: Canon-only rung; the four sibling BRANCHES are still at v2.3.5 and were not ported. That does not affect CI: build_one.sh reconstructs a sibling as the canon tree replayed from patches/ plus overlays/<MODEL>.patch (identity only), so the new wlcsm_bindfix package reaches all five models straight from the series. cut_rung step 7 confirms it: this rung touches 8 files and overlaps no overlay, so no overlay regeneration is required and none was done. The sibling branches will pick the package up on their next port_sibling_v2 run - worth a dry run first, since a brand-new top-level package directory has not previously been exercised through the protect classifier. NOT BUILT and NOT on hardware on any model.

releases.summary: Five-part maintenance rung, all of it driven by field reports of features that reported success while doing nothing. Warden's blocked-hit counters now survive a reboot and a firmware upgrade, per-country included, and gain a user-selectable retention window; the counters had no per-country persistence at all and the total was banked only on a path that the reboot and Save-and-Apply flows never took. UPnP mappings are restored after every firewall rebuild instead of being silently flushed and never re-added -- the daemon kept reporting them as live, which is why this read as 'UPnP is broken' -- and the default daemon is now an IGD:2 device, with new refusal of UPnP/PCP mappings on the router's own VPN, SSH and web-admin ports. The DHCP Leases page resolves its Device Name column from custom_clientlist server-side rather than from networkmap's volatile client table, and both the device name and the client-chosen DHCP hostname are now escaped for the JavaScript and HTML sinks they land in. The Smart Connect page explains its '- -' columns instead of looking broken, and an unclosed table cell there is fixed. Finally, first-boot enforcement moves out of page JavaScript and into httpd: the credential and Wi-Fi steps could previously be walked past by typing the URL of any of the 117 pages that do not load state.js, and the Wi-Fi step was never reached at all because the credential step exited to a page whose own guard did not check it. NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
releases.models_note: Fleet-ported 2026-08-11, same day as the rung. Order followed was rung -> sibling ports -> overlays, which is not negotiable: regenerating an overlay before the port writes one that REVERTS the rung on every sibling and still applies cleanly, which is the 2026-08-10 regression. Ports run in git worktrees under /home/reaper/port (the four per-model WSL instances were deleted 2026-08-10; port_sibling_v2.sh takes REAPER_TREE). Each model got two commits: the dict supplement, then the guarded overlay port. The dict step is mandatory here because port_sibling_v2 protects ??.dict as per-model identity and this rung ADDS tokens (RWDN_56..68, RDST_64, RFB_15/16) -- without it the siblings render raw <#token#> text on the Warden, Storage and first-boot pages. Verified per model rather than trusting the checkout: EN.dict 6312 lines matching canon, RFB_15 present, DE.dict RWDN_56 present, and a single distinct line count across all 24 (stale dicts are internally lockstep too, so lockstep alone proves nothing). Every port guard passed on all four -- branch, target.mak block, BUILD_NAME, router-sysdep base, HAS_6G band match, banner content and banner references, SAMBA4 token -- and each reported post-commit parity of 0 unsynced shared files against canon. 20 shared files synced per model. Sibling tips: rt-be86u e1a4d04afa, rt-be88u af418c1f82, gt-be98 5d7da42f7f, gt-be98-pro 18f54e5a77. All four overlays regenerated from the new tips (4 substantive lines each, the banner swap) and the identity gate passes: GT-BE98 19 files, GT-BE98_PRO 26, RT-BE86U 14, RT-BE88U 22, identity only. NOT BUILT on any model -- source ports only.

releases.summary: Single-defect release: a framed-layout regression introduced by v2.3.3's own overlay re-anchoring, found on metal within hours of flashing it. Reaper_QoS.asp and Reaper_Traffic.asp rendered oversized and clipped at the right edge of a 1080p screen with no scrollbar. The v2.3.3 rule listed .flyout among the full-frame overlays and forced the whole list to position:absolute; the FAQ fly-out is not a full-frame overlay but a 440px side panel PARKED OFF-SCREEN at right:-460px. A parked absolute panel counts towards the framed document's scrollWidth and a parked fixed one does not, so the document reported +460px, the shell's frame-grow widened #page_frame to match, and every grid stretched to the wider frame - the 'zoomed in' symptom - putting the right-hand column outside the window. Only those two pages carry a fly-out, which is exactly why only those two broke. Fixed by keeping .flyout position:fixed while still anchoring its top/height to the visible slice; inside a frame that never scrolls internally the two resolve against the same box, so the fly-out still opens on screen. Measured alternatives, recorded so they are not retried: with an absolute panel right:-460px adds 460, transform:translateX(100%) adds 440, and visibility:hidden changes nothing - only a clipping ancestor prevents it, and clipping the framed root would break the deliberate frame-widening that lets wide stock tables pan. Second, .stage now carries min-width:0: it is a grid item whose default min-width:auto refuses to shrink below its content, so overflow-x:auto could never scroll and the page clipped SILENTLY instead of showing a horizontal scrollbar; any future frame-grow now pans visibly. Verified with a negative control in a mock render of the real shell, both pages - broken: doc 1603->2063 (+460), frame widened to 1603px, flyout absolute; fixed: doc 1143->1143, frame not widened, flyout fixed - matching the owner's on-router reading of doc 1405->1865 with ASIDE#flyout.flyout as the outermost offender. v2.3.3 was built and flashed before this was found, so the fix ships as its own version rather than redefining v2.3.3. NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
releases.models_note: Fleet-ported 2026-08-11, immediately after the v2.3.3 port. 7 shared files synced per model with post-commit parity 0 unsynced shared files against canon on all four; dicts already in sync (this rung changes none) and lockstep at 6296 lines. Port commits: rt-be86u d40c4c1e7e, rt-be88u 6f249685f8, gt-be98 e35d4d76b3, gt-be98-pro 8dfab50d63. UNLIKE v2.3.3, the overlays DID need regenerating: reaper_shell.asp is in every overlays/<MODEL>.patch file set, so changing it shifted the banner line's hunk context - 2 substantive lines per model. All four regenerated and re-checked with the same identity gate CI runs (build-scripts/ci/check_overlays.py): identity only, no shared-code reversion. Sibling builds unvalidated on metal.

releases.summary: Security + de-cloud rung, built and metal-validated on RT-BE96U. Every remaining admin-browser request to the ASUS CDN is gone from the files that ship on this model, verified against the staged filesystem rather than the source tree: client_function.js leaked the name of every ASUS-made LAN device out of the admin browser and wrote the fetched icon into custom_usericon (49 shipped pages load it; an earlier pass fixed only the dashboard copy, which does not ship); the AdGuard banner was fetched from the CDN with the bundled copy wired only as an error fallback, so every visit to that page announced itself before quietly falling back; collected_FAQ, DNS_List, extend_sdn_scenarios, ui-model-name, extend_model_icon, tz_db and pppIspList_V2 now treat the bundled /ajax/ copy as authoritative; GameProfile.asp no longer fetches from ASUS and no longer re-arms itself every 5 seconds forever on failure; Open NAT, IPTV and VPN partner-server lists resolve locally. Per-game artwork removed outright (104 rules, 414 lines) - publisher-owned game art hosted by ASUS, not ours to re-host in a redistributed image, and after the CDN urls were dropped every rule pointed at the same bundled placeholder anyway. QoS: the imq0 ingress redirect is no longer emitted for the hardware engines, where only the tc/HTB engine builds the qdisc it feeds - metal showed 4,619 packets through a redirect that could never shape anything. rexport: values reached a curl -K config unvalidated, where a double quote closes the url string and a following 'output = <path>' directive is an arbitrary file write as root; validated at the httpd layer plus a runtime guard in the generated script. rmcpd: ASUS '>'-delimited security tuples walked through the structural secret scrub, so a live PSK could reach an operator transcript via the lab exec tool. rwatch: the armed log line hardcoded /jffs/rwatch even when the dump root is relocated to the durable store. Native firewall Phase 1 scaffolding is carried but inert - reaper_fw.c is not referenced by rc/Makefile, the page is unwired, and reaper_fw_enable defaults to 0. Second cut of this rung (2026-08-11, patches 0380-0388), all browser- and accounting-side: the post-flash wait doubled its poll chain every round - a failed XHR fires both readystatechange and error, so each round scheduled two successors and the tab genuinely locked up after a firmware upgrade, which is the real cause behind the 'frozen browser' reports (an escape-less veil was a second, lesser defect fixed earlier). Framed overlays - Please Wait, countdowns, progress bars - now anchor to the shell's visible slice rather than the framed document, so they centre on screen instead of in the iframe's viewport. QoS ships the owner's validated classful profile as the type-11 default (rates, weighted/priority mix, class names, preset rules) and the DSCP map is corrected - CS4/AF4x had been landing in Streaming and CS3/AF3x in Gaming, inverted against the class names; preset rules no longer classify by transferred bytes, which had been demoting long-lived streams into the bulk queue. A stored XSS in the client-picker dropdown is closed: the value crossed two parsers - HTML-decoded into an onclick attribute, then parsed as a JS string literal - so HTML-encoding alone was the wrong escape, and a hostile DHCP hostname reached admin context; the last shipped ASUS URL went with it. rtrafd now takes its byte counts from conntrack instead of the accelerator's flow table: /proc/fcache/nflist lists only accelerated flows, so fast downloads - the ones most likely to be offloaded - were the ones most likely to be missing from the traffic list, and br0 under-reported. Plus the Network Map is retired with the dashboard taking its rail slot, the AiMesh node model name centres over its MAC line, and the firmware, Data Export and USB/storage strings are translated across all 24 language packs (dicts in lockstep at 6297 lines). NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
releases.models_note: Fleet-ported 2026-08-11. The four sibling branches were at Reaper_v2.3.1, two rungs behind, so this port carried v2.3.2 and v2.3.3 together: 47 shared files synced per model with port_sibling_v2 (post-commit parity 0 unsynced shared files against canon on all four), plus a separate language-dict sync. The dict step is deliberate - _port_protect classifies *.dict as protected, which is right for a same-version port but would have shipped raw <#TOKEN#> placeholders and English text in 24 languages across a version jump; verified additive-safe first (zero keys exist in a sibling dict that canon lacks, no sibling-side differing value carries model identity). All four dict sets are in lockstep at 6296 lines. Port commits: rt-be86u 523aee1792, rt-be88u 725b7296fb, gt-be98 11d7bb86e6, gt-be98-pro fd1c4e26b4, each followed by its dict commit. OVERLAYS NEEDED NO CHANGE, and this was proven rather than assumed: regenerating overlays/<MODEL>.patch from the ported branches reproduces the shipped file byte-for-byte except for 4 `index` blob-hash lines per model, the patch content being one banner-filename swap per file; CI applies overlays with `git apply --binary --whitespace=nowarn` and no --3way, so those hashes are never read. The decisive check: the published 388-patch series was replayed onto the pinned base and all four SHIPPED overlays apply clean to that exact tree (b034902b69, matching source_tree_from_series). Sibling builds are unvalidated on metal.

releases.summary: Fix rung. Reaper_Firmware.asp's flash overlay could trap the user with no way out (full-viewport click blocker, no dismiss path, two code paths that raised it and returned) - now escapable, with a heartbeat and an error guard, and the false 'image rejected' window widened from ~2 to ~5 min. QoS end-to-end review: qos_dscp_wmm now opt-in (it defaulted on and promoted all sub-512KB web traffic to Wi-Fi AC_VO), qos_default corrected to the class actually named Default, the DSCP->class map un-inverted, committed rates budgeted to 85% so qid0/qid6 keep a share, both hardware engines refuse to arm with no upload bandwidth, plus idempotence and tmctl error logging for the classful engine. Backlog sweep: QOSDIAG-1, B3-SEC-002 (shell injection via vpnc region/conntype), B5-SEC-002 (constant-time password compare), A3-REL-008 (rwatch dump rate-limit). NO IMAGES YET - this entry records the source rung; image hashes are added when the build ships.
releases.models_note: The published patch series is the RT-BE96U line. None of this rung's files appear in any overlays/<MODEL>.patch file set (verified 2026-08-10), so the sibling overlays are unchanged and every model picks these fixes up from the series.

releases.summary: Native firmware page rung: Reaper_Firmware.asp (Phase 2 - check, download, verify and flash from the router GUI) plus the update-check path fix so the check never routes through cfg_mnt/ASUS. Shipped fleet-wide (all five models, both variants, 19/19 on the verify gate) and published as five GitHub releases. This is the first release whose full patch series applies end-to-end onto the pinned base: patches 0246/0247/0252 (the v1.8.6a banner rename and version bump, and the v1.8.6c version bump) had never been extracted, which broke the replay at old patch 0247 for every release from v1.8.6a onward.
releases.models_note: The published patch series is the RT-BE96U line; siblings are produced by porting the shared code onto each per-model branch, so they are not independently patch-reproducible. The image SHAs above are RT-BE96U; per-model sums are in each SHA256SUMS-<MODEL>-Reaper_v2.3.1.txt.

releases.summary: Three field-report fixes: PPPoE baby-jumbo MTU applied to the WAN page variant that actually ships on MULTISERVICE_WAN builds (the v2.1.3 raise had landed on the non-shipped base page; both silent 1492 clamps now fire only when the WAN MTU was deliberately lowered), a self-recovering first-boot credential page (leaves on load when the credential step is already done; a rejected chpass re-probes live state and finishes when the password actually applied - closes the 'won't accept anything' loop), and rtrafd JFFS/USB history persistence (late store attach with 15-min retry so a hotplug-mounted USB store is restored instead of overwritten; never saves over an unloaded db - preserves .prev; USB saves every 15 min, JFFS stays hourly). Built + shipped on all five models in two parallel waves on the new per-model build fleet.
releases.models_note: Built + shipped on all five models (both variants each, all 17/17 on the verify gate). The image SHAs and source-tree hash above are the RT-BE96U reference; the patch series is RT-BE96U-only, and the siblings are produced by porting the shared code onto each per-model branch (banner/target.mak/blob overlay), so they are not independently patch-reproducible. Per-model image SHAs are in each SHA256SUMS-<MODEL>-Reaper_v2.1.5.txt on the release ladder.

releases.summary: Factory-reset credential dead-end fix (login routes a default-password box to the single Reaper first-boot page instead of racing the stock ASUS password page), WireGuard peer-row edit-toggle unclip/center, and the OpenVPN version label corrected to 2.7.5 (a stale generated build file had frozen it at 2.7.4; the binary was already 2.7.5). Built + shipped on all five models.
releases.models_note: Built + shipped on all five models (both variants each, all 17/17 on the verify gate). The image SHAs and source-tree hash above are the RT-BE96U reference; the patch series is RT-BE96U-only, and the siblings are produced by porting the shared code onto each per-model branch (banner/target.mak/blob overlay), so they are not independently patch-reproducible. Per-model image SHAs are in each SHA256SUMS-<MODEL>-Reaper_v2.1.4.txt on the release ladder.

releases.summary: Connections 'Quick Look' default view + Advanced toggle with device-name resolution, RFC 4638 baby-jumbo PPPoE MTU in the WAN GUI, an apostrophe-in-name stored-XSS fix on the stock client list (patch 0311), and three UI touch-ups (Wireless Professional raw-nvram-name drop, AI Advisor intro completion, dashboard SSID mixed-case). RT-BE96U only.
Asuswrt-Merlin 3006.102.8 carry-forward (OpenVPN 2.7.5, dropbear/miniupnpd/strongswan, IPv6 prefix fixes, webui) - 19 upstream commits cherry-picked; no Reaper feature changes.
Error-message localization, structural AI-Advisor redaction + truncation-to-valid-JSON, esc() defense-in-depth, batched Warden feed load, three UI viewport fixes, Channel-Lock confirmation.
Pre-release six-agent code-review hardening pass; three more pages fully localized. Fleet release (all five models).
